A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the contractile elements are not simply on or off, but are regulated by a variety of mechanisms.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the myosin light-chain kinase system plays a major role in regulating smooth muscle contractility, but that it is not the only system that can do this.

the smooth muscle contractile apparatus is a highly complex, regulated molecular motor, and that the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control the motor's function have been conserved throughout evolution.

the contractile machinery of vascular smooth muscle is not as simple as previously thought, and the complexity is likely to have important physiological consequences for the regulation of vascular tone and blood pressure.
